{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeAl4zQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHh2aw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 269, "title": "Prevent in-page microphone icon from covering existing website buttons and controls", "body": "## Problem

The existing Web-page voice-typing microphone icon can visually cover **buttons and other interactive controls already belonging to the website**, making those controls difficult or impossible to click. This is not acceptable for a page-injected utility.

Current implementation in `extension/web-voice-content.js`, `position()` (approximately lines 59–125):
- Places a fixed-position, very high z-index icon near the focused editable field.
- Samples potential obstructions using `document.elementsFromPoint()` and tries a number of right/left/above/below positions.
- **Always picks the least-bad candidate even if every candidate overlaps** other page UI. The non-interactive status bubble also needs to respect page controls.
- Placement runs during scrolling and viewport changes, but collision handling is best-effort rather than a safety guarantee.

## Approved UX / required behavior

1. Prefer placing the existing mic icon **to the right of the focused field**, when unobstructed; otherwise look at reasonable left/above/below positions close to that field.
2. Treat the site's existing **buttons, links, inputs, editable content, menus, labels and other interactive controls** as obstructions. Do not cover them with the mic's visual area or clickable hit target. Check both geometry and actual hit-testing/stacking as appropriate; handle shadow DOM, clipping, dense layouts and viewport edges conservatively.
3. **Idle / not recording:** when no safe, visible position exists, **do not show the mic icon**. Never fall back to covering an existing website button merely because the candidate has the lowest collision score.
4. **Preparing / recording / stopping:** preserve a usable way to cancel/stop the current voice session. If placement near the field becomes unsafe, relocate the same existing control to an unobstructed location in the viewport where possible. Do not silently hide the only stop control or make it unclickable; handle cases with no safe location deliberately without obscuring critical site controls. Avoid introducing an extra permanent toolbar or page layout modifications.
5. On resize, scrolling, visual viewport changes, element movement and dynamic page updates, reassess placement so the icon does not become an obstruction after initial display. Avoid layout thrashing or unnecessarily expensive whole-page scans.
6. The small recording/error status label must also **not block native page interactions** (it is already non-interactive) and should avoid visually obscuring controls when it can; clamp safely inside viewport.
7. Never insert padding, wrap/move the site's own DOM, reserve space by altering the site's CSS, or replace existing controls. Preserve field focus/caret and existing state/Stop behavior.
8. Keep accessibility (keyboard reachable mic when visible, meaningful status, contrast, touch target, reduced motion), positioning for scrolled/offscreen targets, and behavior on narrow viewports.

## Implementation guidance

- Scope change chiefly to `extension/web-voice-content.js` and relevant Web voice UI tests.
- Replace “pick minimum obstruction score regardless of collisions” with **safe-candidate acceptance** for idle display. Candidate testing should avoid false collisions caused by the widget itself and avoid false safety caused by partial sampling or overlays.
- Use an explicit, predictable active-session fallback if the normal field-adjacent candidates are unsafe. Do not silently abandon recording or unexpectedly refocus the field.
- Preserve the in-page mic’s left/right-click graph selection and non-switching behavior being implemented in #266, opt-in/permission policy from #247, and no extension-owned recurring recording window from #263.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Web page with a button immediately next to an editable input never has that original button visually covered or have its click intercepted by the idle mic.
- [ ] If free space exists to the right, place the mic there; if not, choose safe left/above/below location.
- [ ] When no safe location exists in idle state, hide the mic rather than overlay a site button.
- [ ] During active recording or preparation, the original Stop/Cancel remains accessible when nearby placement becomes unsafe; no duplicate icon/session or accidental site interaction.
- [ ] Dynamic page layout, scrolling and resizing do not cause the icon or status label to obscure existing interactive UI.
- [ ] No host-page DOM/CSS reflow hacks and no new permanent controls.
- [ ] Automated browser/UI tests cover button adjacency, tightly packed fields, viewport edges, layout changes, active recording fallback, and click-through behavior. Record tests actually run.

## Scope

Positioning/obstruction avoidance **only**; do not redesign the Graph Library, graph selection menus, runtime engine or microphone permission flow. Related: #247, #249, #263, #266.
